'In 662 BCE, Xing was heavily threatened by the Red Di tribes'; 'Duke Huan of Qi relocated Xing southeast to a place known as Yiyi (modern day Liaocheng City, Shandong)'. Reviewer (ea-01-x, 2026-10-19): confidence 2, not 3: the page dates the Red Di threat to 662 BCE but gives no year for the relocation to Yiyi (the sentence follows the 662 one undated).

notes: Page opened (1 of 1-2): Xing (state). Wikidata id left null (unreachable). START -1043 is the end of the page's 'between 1046 and 1043 BCE'; the infobox says only 'the 11th century BCE'. The 662 loss of the Xingtai plain is a bridge (page silent on the holder; plausibly the Red Di) and the gain of Yiyi names Qi only as the arranger. The wey dossier (ea-01-c) already carries the 635 gain with counterpart xing. AREA: none; no Cliopatria row. A second page (Wey or Qi) would be needed for the 662 aftermath.
